claims.text: As-fabricated HfNbTiVAl10 has a hierarchical heterostructure.
The hierarchical heterostructure includes variable grain sizes.
The hierarchical heterostructure includes variable interface misorientations, phase fractions, and defect densities.
A convolutional neural network trained on systematically sampled EBSD and TEM images can predict Young's modulus in HfNbTiVAl10.
The imaging-based convolutional neural network can predict yield strength in HfNbTiVAl10.
The imaging-based convolutional neural network can predict fracture-related behavior in HfNbTiVAl10.
Grain-size distributions, interface misorientations, phase fractions, and local defect densities mediate the stress-strain response.
The CNN can learn correlations between the identified microstructural descriptors and mechanical responses.
The learned correlations capture hierarchical heterostructure effects.
The CNN bypasses explicit simulation of multiscale interactions.
By bypassing explicit multiscale simulation, the CNN reduces computational overhead.
The CNN will improve yield-strength prediction accuracy by approximately 30% relative to established multiphysics simulations.
The CNN will improve fracture-onset prediction accuracy by approximately 30% relative to established multiphysics simulations.
The CNN will reduce computation time by up to one order of magnitude relative to traditional simulation methods.
Predictions may become inaccurate if the training images do not represent the relevant range of microstructural variation.
Generalization may fail under non-standard deformation conditions or environments outside room temperature.
Computational speed gains may depend on dataset quality and available computational resources.
